Nonlinear Dynamics and Primary Resonance Characteristics of Spiral Bevel Gear Systems
recent_works.venue: International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos
recent_works.abstract: This paper investigates the nonlinear vibration characteristics of spiral bevel gear transmission systems. A dynamic model was established by incorporating key nonlinear factors, including bearing support forces, time-varying mesh stiffness, gear backlash, mesh damping, and static transmission error. The system’s vibration differential equations were solved using the Runge–Kutta method. The nonlinear dynamic behavior under varying parameters was analyzed through time-domain waveforms, frequency spectra, phase portraits, Poincaré sections, bifurcation diagrams, wavelet time-frequency plots, and Lyapunov exponent spectra. Employing the multiscale method, the primary resonance equation was derived to examine the influence of mesh damping, mesh stiffness, and external load fluctuations on the system’s primary resonance characteristics. The results indicate that spiral bevel gear systems exhibit significant nonlinearity. As the excitation frequency or static transmission error increases, the system transitions from periodic to chaotic motion. recent_works.title: Configuration, snap-through and free vibration of bistable asymmetric composite laminated cantilever plate for wind turbine blade skin
recent_works.abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the stable configurations, snap-through behavior, and small-amplitude free vibrations of bistable asymmetric composite laminated cantilever plates, motivated by their potential application in load-adaptive wind turbine blade designs. An advanced theoretical framework is developed by combining the classical laminated plate theory, von Kármán geometric nonlinearity, the Rayleigh–Ritz method, and Hamilton’s principle, from which the governing differential equations of motion are derived. The model’s accuracy is confirmed through finite element simulations and experimental results. The potential energy function is employed to characterize bistability, while the Jacobian matrix is used to assess configuration stability. Under transverse excitation applied at two corners of the free edge, the critical snap-through loads are predicted, and curvature evolution during transitions is quantified. Parametric studies reveal the influence of aspect ratio and thickness on snap-through thresholds and fundamental frequency variations. Investigations of the Vibrational Design and Nonlinear Dynamic for the Three-Phase Graphene and Fiber-Reinforced Aluminum-based Laminated Composite Cantilever Trapezoidal Wing Plate
recent_works.venue: International Journal of Structural Stability and Dynamics
recent_works.abstract: For the increasing demand of better dynamic performance and fuel efficiency in next-generation aircraft, the structural design for the wing plate needs to consider lightweight materials with superior mechanical properties. With high mechanical strength and low mass density, graphene-reinforced composites represent an excellent option for lightweight structural design. In this paper, comparative design analyses are conducted for a three-phase graphene and titanium fiber-reinforced (G-TFR) aluminum-based cantilevered trapezoidal laminated composite wing plate based on its natural vibration characteristics. Moreover, the nonlinear dynamic responses under dual-parameter excitations are systematically investigated to reveal the complex vibration behavior. The mechanical properties of the three-phase G-TFR aluminum-based composites are evaluated using the Halpin–Tsai model combined with the elastic theory.
